claims.note: Set-identical to the artifact list, derived independently. MT 24:1 BELONGS: its skeleton carries the year word בשנה plus the month terms בחדש and לחדש plus the day term בעשור - it satisfies the rule on three independent terms, not one. The rule is sound and, for the dateline output, robust: I ran the year test two ways - a strictly prefix-anchored token and a bare substring - and got the SAME 14 either way, because the two verses that separate those readings (26:10, 46:13) carry no month or day term. False-negative probe: every other verse in Ezekiel containing חדש/חדשים/עשור - MT 18:31, 36:26, 39:12, 39:14, 45:17, 45:18, 45:20, 45:21, 45:25, 46:1, 46:3, 46:6 - carries no year word, and each is either חדש meaning 'new' (18:31, 36:26, 'a new heart') or a cultic/calendar month, so none is a missed oracle dateline. The structural rule also survives MT 26:1 and 32:17, which give no month ordinal at all and are caught on לחדש alone - the cardinal-stem rule this repair replaced would have been fragile there too, not only at 24:1.

claims.my_count: 7 verses under a loose (substring) year match; 5 under the literally-stated 'prefix optional' rule
claims.note: The MT 26:10 sub-claim is CONFIRMED outright, and it is the important half. Ezek 26:10 reads 'תרעשנה' (your walls shall shake); the token skeleton is תרעשנה, a 3fp imperfect of רעש, in which the sequence שנה spans the root-final shin plus the -nun-he suffix. There is no year word in 26:10 and no month or day term. It is a substring artifact, exactly as the repair says. The PARTLY is about framing, not arithmetic - no verse is missing and none is extra. (a) The JSON key 'year_word_but_not_a_dateline' and the TOOLKIT sentence 'Seven verses carry one and are NOT datelines' are literally untrue of 26:10, which carries no year word at all; both texts correct themselves in the very next clause ('one substring artifact' / 'FALSE POSITIVE of the year regex alone'), so the artifact is self-consistent, but the label and the list are describing different things. (b) MT 46:13 is שנתו - שנת plus a 3ms SUFFIX. The rule as stated ('שנה/שנת, prefix optional') does not reach a suffixed form; 46:13 enters only under a substring or suffix-tolerant match. So the figure 7 is the output of the loose reading while the stated rule describes the anchored reading, which yields 5. Recommend the artifact say plainly that this list is the residue of the loose year regex - 6 genuine year words plus 1 substring artifact - which is what it actually is.

claims.my_count: strict 39 / vayehi-any 41 / hayah-perfect 7; verse counts and occurrence counts coincide at 39, 41, 7
claims.note: All three verse lists are set-identical to the artifact. MT 12:8 infixes בבקר ('in the morning'), MT 24:1 infixes the full ninth-year dateline, and both still end in לאמר. Two closure checks I added: the strict and loose sets differ in one direction only (STRICT minus LOOSE is empty), and 41 + 7 = 48 with the two sets disjoint, which equals every occurrence in the book of 'דבר יהוה אלי' - nothing falls outside the three-way split. That independently matches the artifact's family_total_distinct = 48. I also re-ran the perfect form with a word-start anchor so היה could not match inside a longer word: still 7, the same 7. One robustness note with no impact here: my loose count simply drops the adjacency requirement rather than modelling 'infixed temporal phrase', which is broader than the gloss; it coincides only because no ויהי דבר יהוה אלי verse in Ezekiel lacks לאמר somewhere in the verse (I checked: zero such verses). On a book where that failed, the two definitions would diverge.

findings_outside_the_five_claims.where: ezek_device_inventory.json key 'calendar_dates_not_datelines' (count 3) and TOOLKIT.md line 174 ('THREE date formulae that are NOT datelines')
findings_outside_the_five_claims.finding: The enumeration MT 45:20, 45:21, 45:25 appears to UNDERCOUNT by one. MT 45:18 reads בראשון באחד לחדש - month ordinal plus day plus לחדש, and no year word - which is a FULLER date formula than MT 45:20 (בשבעה בחדש, day only). If 45:20 qualifies, 45:18 qualifies a fortiori.
findings_outside_the_five_claims.why_it_matters: MT 45:18 is the chapter-45 verse most likely to be misread as a unit onset, because it pairs that date formula with the messenger formula כה אמר אדני יהוה - the artifact's own thus_says_the_lord_yhwh list includes Ezek.45.18. The warning list exists precisely to stop a false boundary inside the law block, and it omits the strongest candidate for one.
findings_outside_the_five_claims.impact_on_the_five_claims: none - MT 45:18 has no year word, so the dateline count of 14 is unaffected

own tokeniser: strip every character that is not a Hebrew letter U+05D0-U+05EA (thus removing all U+0591-U+05C7 points and accents) to a consonantal skeleton, collapse whitespace, split on space; then require a year token AND a month/day token in the same verse. Ran the year test twice - anchored ^[prefix]{0,3}(שנה|שנת)$ and a bare substring - and compared the two outputs. Separately probed every verse in the book containing חדש/חדשים/עשור for a missed dateline.
